subtitle: "A worked volume-conduction-robust connectivity case on real EEG, checked against scipy"
categories: [eeg, connectivity, phase-synchronization, pli, volume-conduction, validated]
author: "Yusuke Matsui"
date: "2026-09-04"

> **What this case shows** — the [sibling case](../eeg-plv-alpha-eegmmidb/index.qmd) found a
> high occipital alpha **PLV** (O1-Oz = 0.92). But is that genuine neural coupling, or just
> **volume conduction** — one source seen by two nearby electrodes, plus the common reference?
> PLV can't tell: it counts zero-lag coupling as real. The **phase-lag index** (Stam 2007) can —
> **PLI = |mean(sign(sin(φₓ − φᵧ)))|** counts only a *consistent non-zero* phase lag, so it is
> ~0 for zero-lag coupling. On the same O1-Oz pair, the alpha **PLI is just 0.016** — the strong
> PLV collapses, revealing the "synchronization" is dominated by near-zero-lag coupling. And the
> measure is trustworthy: on constructed signals it recovers the contrast exactly (zero-lag →
> PLV 0.99 but **PLI 0.01**; genuine lagged coupling → **PLI 1.0**; independent → both 0),
> reproduces an independent `scipy` Hilbert-band PLI, and its sign formula is exact.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for volume-conduction-robust phase coupling: `phaseLagIndex(x, y, sr, freq_band)`
→ read `pli`; compare it to the PLV to see how much coupling is zero-lag.
**Way of thinking** — a *high PLV with a low PLI* is the signature of volume conduction:
strong phase consistency, but at ~zero lag. PLI keeps only lead/lag-consistent coupling.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioCrossModal::phaseLagIndex()`; `weightedPLI()` for the debiased,
less-noisy variant (Vinck 2011).
:::

## Proposition

On the real O1-Oz pair whose alpha PLV is 0.92, the PLI is only 0.016 — the coupling is mostly
volume conduction. `phaseLagIndex` reproduces an independent scipy PLI, has an exact sign
formula, and recovers the volume-conduction contrast (zero-lag → PLI 0.01 while PLV 0.99;
lagged → PLI 1.0).

## Question & goal

**The question is whether a high PLV means real coupling — and PLI is how you check.** Volume
conduction inflates PLV (and coherence) but not PLI. The goal is to validate `phaseLagIndex`
(against scipy, an exact formula, and known signals) and use it to reinterpret the O1-Oz alpha.

## Challenge & approach

PLI band-passes and Hilbert-phases each signal, then takes the consistency of the *sign* of the
phase difference. We compute it with `phaseLagIndex`, re-compute it with scipy, and run it on
constructed signals with a known coupling type (zero-lag / lagged / independent).

```
O1, Oz EEG → phaseLagIndex(alpha) → PLI = 0.016   (vs PLV 0.92)
                    vs scipy (butter+filtfilt+hilbert)        → agreement (~4e-3)
                    vs constructed zero-lag / lagged / indep   → PLI 0.01 / 1.0 / 0.03
```

## Data

**eegmmidb (PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02 (eyes-closed)**, occipital **O1** and
**Oz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked pair the sibling PLV case uses. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: PLV (blue) vs PLI (orange) across four conditions. For the real O1-Oz pair and for constructed zero-lag (volume-conduction) coupling, PLV is high (0.92, 0.99) but PLI is ~0 (0.02, 0.01) — PLI discounts the zero-lag component. For genuinely lagged coupling both are high (PLI 1.0); for independent signals both are ~0. Right: the real O1-Oz alpha phase-difference clusters tightly at ~0 rad — a near-zero lag, which gives a high PLV but a near-zero PLI.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel is the whole story — **high PLV + low PLI = volume
conduction**; the right panel shows why (the O1-Oz phase difference sits at ~0).

| Condition | PLV | PLI |
|---|--:|--:|
| **real O1-Oz alpha** | **0.92** | **0.016** |
| constructed zero-lag (volume conduction) | 0.99 | 0.01 |
| constructed lagged (π/4) | 0.99 | 1.00 |
| constructed independent | 0.02 | 0.03 |

| Validation | Value | Reference |
|---|--:|---|
| PLI vs scipy Hilbert-band (max \|diff\|) | 4e-3 | 0 (agreement) |
| PLI sign-formula residual | 0 | 0 (exact) |

The op recovers the contrast, matches scipy, and reinterprets the O1-Oz alpha as mostly volume
conduction. Values trace to [`artifacts/pli_summary.csv`](artifacts/pli_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

The phase-lag index does what PLV cannot: it discounts zero-lag coupling, and on real occipital
EEG it reveals that a headline alpha PLV of 0.92 is almost entirely volume conduction (PLI 0.016).
The transferable takeaway: **never read a high PLV/coherence as connectivity without checking
PLI/wPLI — a high PLV with a low PLI is the fingerprint of volume conduction — and remember PLI
is conservative (it also discounts genuine zero-lag coupling), so treat it as a lower bound on
lagged interaction, not a verdict.**

## Open questions

- PLI is binary in the sign and can be noisy; the **weighted PLI** (`weightedPLI`, debiased,
  Vinck 2011 — also implemented) weights each phase difference by |sin| and removes the
  sample-size bias for a less noisy VC-robust estimate. A full channel × channel wPLI matrix
  would map the genuinely-*lagged* posterior alpha network (vs the volume-conduction-inflated
  PLV network), and eyes-closed vs eyes-open would test whether that lagged component tracks the
  rhythm. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| phase-lag index (VC-robust) | `phaseLagIndex()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| weighted PLI (debiased, less noisy) | `weightedPLI()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| phase-locking value (compare — VC-sensitive) | `phaseLockingValue()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| magnitude-squared coherence (also VC-sensitive) | `coherence()` | PhysioCrossModal |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **freq_band** — the band to test (here `c(8, 13)`, alpha).
- **compare with PLV** — always: a high PLV + low PLI flags volume conduction; similar PLV and
  PLI suggests genuinely lagged coupling.
- **caveat** — PLI is conservative (discounts *all* near-zero-lag coupling); use `weightedPLI()`
  for a debiased estimate and treat a low PLI as a lower bound on lagged interaction.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioCrossModal)

pli <- phaseLagIndex(o1, oz, sr = 160, freq_band = c(8, 13))$pli   # 0.016
plv <- phaseLockingValue(o1, oz, sr = 160, freq_band = c(8, 13))$plv  # 0.92
# high PLV + low PLI  ->  the alpha coupling is mostly volume conduction

# reproduces an independent scipy Hilbert-band PLI (~4e-3); the sign formula is exact.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/`](artifacts/) — the summary in
[`pli_summary.csv`](artifacts/pli_summary.csv) — and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks each
